newsitem.title: USA: Chicago settles soundproofing lawsuit for $11 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chicago settles soundproofing lawsuit for $11 mln.

text.p: Chicago has agreed to spend an additional $11.4 million this year in soundproofing suburban houses near O'Hare International Airport to resolve a federal lawsuit, a city aviation department spokesman said Wednesday.

The city had planned to spend $21 million soundproofing residences near the airport as part of a multi-year $300 million noise abatement plan, but agreed to accelerate efforts rather than risk delaying the whole project through litigation, Dennis Culloton said.
The work is financed primarily through user fees assessed at O'Hare and Midway Airport with a small contribution from federal airport improvement grants, Culloton said.
U.S. District Judge James Holderman signed off on the settlement with the Village of Bensenville Tuesday. The village had contended that city officials used the program as political leverage.
Chicago anticipates spending another $22 million on the program in 1998 and has not made projections for spending in 1999.
